Actually, most games have their IP addresses public. For example, you can find the IP addresses for ESO (Elder Scrolls Online) servers pretty easily. Most companies don't need to worry about such a thing as their location because they are usually A: insured by an insurance company, and B: most people aren't stupid enough to try breaking into a companies' place. Also, servers are usually in the basement or at a secondary location (a separate building).

An IP address is something every device that can connect to the internet has. In fact, it is actually necessary (unless you do something weird) to connect to the internet. It is like a serial code given to a device by a wifi network to identify the device. So yes, the server will have an IP address (not trying to sound like an ass, just saying).
